summary: Independent adversarial review found no blocker or important issues. 84 rows = 14 donors (7 control, 7 HD) x 2 cell types (fibroblast, iN) x 3 technical replicates, all mapped 1:1 to the 84 PRIDE RAW files. Only minor improvements remain.

reviewer_context.context: fresh reviewer agent without producer transcript; producer report.md not relied upon

spec_compliance.evidence: Templates ms-proteomics + human (declared v1.1.0) are appropriate: human primary dermal fibroblasts and directly converted iNs (not established cell lines). All required columns present; single-row shape per RAW; no duplicate assay names/data files; biological replicate numbered 1-7 restarting per factor group (cell type x disease), consistent with README 'Encoding sample technical and biological replicates'.

ontology_integrity.evidence: Resolved in local OLS cache: CL:0000057 fibroblast, CL:0000540 neuron, UBERON:0002097 skin of body, MONDO:0007739 huntington disease, PATO:0000461 normal, PRIDE:0000627 data-dependent acquisition, PRIDE:0000608 dithiothreitol (DTT), PRIDE:0000599 iodoacetamide (IAA), MS:1002038 label free sample, MS:1002877 Q Exactive HF-X, MS:1001251 Trypsin, MS:1000422 beam-type CID, UNIMOD:1/4/21/35 Acetyl/Carbamidomethyl/Phospho/Oxidation. Labels and accessions match; none obsolete.

source_evidence.evidence: pride.json (accession PXD024286 asserted) and manuscript Methods 'Shotgun proteomic analysis': 7 control + 7 HD lines as fibroblasts and iNs; triplicate injections; Q-Exactive HF-X (PRIDE instrument field says Q Exactive HF but both PRIDE protocol text and paper say HF-X); top-20 DDA, NCE 28; DTT in lysis buffer + IAA; trypsin; PD 2.2 with 10 ppm / 0.02 Da, CAM C fixed, Ox M, Phospho STY, protein N-term Acetyl variable. Disease/cell type from RAW prefixes FBC/FBHD/INC/INHD. sdrf-tools reconcile: every value agrees with the deposit record.

file_mapping.evidence: files_compact.json has 84 RAW + 4 .msf + 1 FASTA. All 84 comment[data file] values match RAW names exactly, no duplicates, no unmatched RAW; assay name == data file stem for every row; 3 runs per source name.

design_consistency.evidence: 28 source names (14 donors x fibroblast/iN), each with technical replicates 1-3; characteristics[individual] links fibroblast and iN of the same donor; factors cell type and disease match characteristics; 7 donors per disease group consistent with paper (C1-C7; HD1-2, HD5-7, HD9-10). Label free, single fraction.

omission_safety.evidence: No unsupported values: age and sex set to 'not available' because file donor codes (C11, CBS, HDKP, HD4 ...) cannot be linked to paper Table 2 (and file code HD4 conflicts with the paper's MS donor list, where HD4 is a female line not used for MS). Omitted-but-available details (adult stage, NCAM+ FACS at 4 weeks) recorded as minor findings.

deterministic_validation.evidence: flock parse_sdrf validate-sdrf -t ms-proteomics -t human --use_ols_cache_only: 'Everything seems to be fine', exit 0. sdrf-tools check --offline: CLEAN, 0 hallucinated, exit 0. sdrf-tools score: 97/100. sdrf-tools reconcile vs pride.json: all values agree.

findings.message: Paper and PRIDE protocol state the HD lines used for MS were 'only males'; HD rows could be annotated 'male' if the producer accepts this cohort-wide universal statement. 'not available' is a defensible conservative choice given the HD4 file-code conflict.
Manifest claim says 'HD rows male' but the SDRF has 'not available' for all rows (the limitations section says the opposite). Align the claim with the artifact.
Recommended column missing; all donors are adults (27-75 y, 'adult dermal fibroblasts'), so 'adult' is supportable.
findings.evidence: manuscript Table 2 and fibroblast source paragraph; sdrf-tools score completeness

findings.message: Paper states iNs were NCAM+ FACS-purified at 4 weeks post-conversion for the transcriptome/proteome analyses; evidence manifest wrongly says conversion length not stated. Optionally capture in a comment/characteristics column.
'28% NCE' deviates from spec pattern '{value} {unit}' (e.g. '28 NCE'); validator accepted it.
